findings.title: AssignmentSource.queued default is a shared class-level value
findings.body: The field default `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the class body is executed at module import time, not per instance. Every AssignmentSource constructed without an explicit `queued` (which is every call site in this PR, including `from_integration`) shares the exact same datetime object captured at import time. The fix is to use `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance gets the timestamp of its own creation. The current `test_to_dict` only asserts the field is non-null, so this regression goes undetected.

findings.title: sync_assignee_outbound is invoked with assignment_source kwarg that concrete subclasses may reject
findings.body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue, user, assign=assign, assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)`. The abstract definition in `IssueSyncIntegration` still relies on `**kwargs` to absorb extra arguments, but concrete subclasses (e.g. the Jira/GitHub/etc. integrations) typically override `sync_assignee_outbound(self, external_issue, user, assign=True)` without `**kwargs` and without an `assignment_source` parameter. Calling those overrides with the new kwarg will raise `TypeError: ... unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source'`, breaking assignee sync for every integration. The mock-based test `test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign` does not exercise real subclass signatures and therefore does not catch this. Either add `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None` to the abstract signature (as was done for `sync_status_outbound`) and update every concrete override, or remove the kwarg from the call site until those overrides are updated.

findings.title: from_dict silently returns None on deserialization failure, bypassing cycle protection
findings.body: `from_dict` swallows any `ValueError`/`TypeError` and returns `None`. The only consumer (`sync_assignee_outbound`) treats `None` as 'no source' and then runs `should_sync` without the cycle guard, so any malformed or schema-drifted `assignment_source_dict` silently disables the very protection this PR introduces and re-enables the original sync loop. The dict is produced by the same code path that consumes it, so silent fallback is risky. Consider raising (so Celery retries / surfaces a metric) or at least logging a warning when reconstruction fails, and updating callers/tests accordingly.

findings.title: sync_status_outbound signature change is unused dead code
findings.body: `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_status_outbound` is updated to accept `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None`, but no call site in this PR (or anywhere visible in the diff) ever constructs or forwards an `AssignmentSource` for the status path, and no caller of `sync_status_outbound` is modified. The parameter is dead until the status sync cycle is actually fixed, and it is inconsistent with `sync_assignee_outbound` (which still relies on `**kwargs` for the same purpose). Either thread `AssignmentSource` through the inbound status flow and add the cycle guard there, or revert the abstract signature change to avoid misleading readers.

findings.title: No coverage for deassign path with matching AssignmentSource
findings.body: A new test `test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration` was added to verify that `assign` skips outbound sync when the source integration matches the target. The equivalent unassign path (`GroupAssignee.objects.deassign(...)` followed by `sync_group_assignee_outbound`) is not covered — the only deassign test (`test_assignee_sync_outbound_unassign`) only asserts the no-source case. Add a parallel test that passes an `AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` to `deassign` and asserts `mock_sync_assignee_outbound.assert_not_called()`, since `GroupAssigneeManager.deassign` also forwards `assignment_source` to `sync_group_assignee_outbound`.
